tweets: Why is VendraRx launching with a waitlist? It’s about clinical infrastructure minimums — and refusing to pay for idle capacity until we have the patient volume to support it. Here’s why that matters: (thread)

Telehealth peptide therapy demands more than just a provider. Labs, follow-up, physician supervision, and 503A compounding all cost. Building idle capacity before demand exists drives up per-patient costs unnecessarily.

We’re not a refill mill or a research-peptide vendor. Clinical operations require scale. Waiting until we have the patient base ensures we can sustainably invest in infrastructure without compromising quality.
Our approach: secure the minimum patient volume first, then build clinical capacity around it. This keeps unit economics intact and ensures we don’t cut corners.
Peptide therapy is clinician-determined, not one-size-fits-all. Our model prioritizes sustainable, physician-supervised care over scaling prematurely.
